RFP context: RFP ID:** Public Health Labs-RFP-2022-HEPC-019 | Issue Date:** June 20, 2022 | Federal Sponsor:** Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / DVHAP | Program Area:** Viral Hepatitis — Hepatitis C Elimination

Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection affects an estimated 2.4 million Americans and is now curable with direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) achieving >95% sustained virologic response. The United States has set a national goal to eliminate HCV as a public health threat by 2030. A critical barrier to elimination is the testing-to-treatment gap: many individuals who test HCV antibody positive are never confirmed by RNA testing and never linked to treatment.

State public health laboratories can play a transformative role by offering reflex HCV RNA testing (automatic RNA testing following a positive antibody) and integrating genotyping to guide treatment selection. This RFP funds laboratories to implement or expand reflex HCV RNA testing at no cost to patients, with priority on populations most affected by HCV — persons who inject drugs, individuals experiencing homelessness, and incarcerated populations.

RFP context: RFP ID:** Public Health Labs-RFP-2024-PERTUSSIS-045 | Issue Date:** August 5, 2024 | Federal Sponsor:** Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / NCIRD / DBD | Program Area:** Vaccine-Preventable Disease — Pertussis Surveillance

Pertussis (whooping cough) resurged significantly in the United States in 2024, with case counts on track to exceed 30,000 — the highest in over a decade — driven by waning immunity from acellular pertussis vaccines, increased detection from molecular methods, and school-age outbreak clusters. Bordetella pertussis strain evolution, including the spread of prn-deficient (pertactin-negative) strains that may evade vaccine immunity, requires laboratory-based genomic characterization to track vaccine-driven selection pressure. State laboratories serve as the primary confirmatory testing resource for pertussis outbreak investigation and must support both diagnostic surge and genomic epidemiology.

RFP context: RFP ID:** Public Health Labs-RFP-2021-STI-015 | Issue Date:** September 20, 2021 | Federal Sponsor:** Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / DSTDP | Program Area:** STI Laboratory — Gonorrhea AMR Surveillance

Neisseria gonorrhoeae has demonstrated resistance to every antibiotic class recommended for treatment over its history. Ceftriaxone, the last remaining recommended single-agent therapy in the United States, now faces documented reduced susceptibility and confirmed treatment failures internationally. The Gonococcal Isolate Surveillance Project (GISP) and its successor Strengthening the U.S. Response to Resistant Gonorrhea (SURRG) depend on state public health laboratory capacity to culture, perform antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), and conduct WGS on gonorrhea isolates from sentinel sites.

This RFP funds state public health laboratories to maintain and expand GISP/SURRG participation, implement WGS for gonococcal isolates, and support state STI programs with laboratory diagnostics.

The Laboratory Response Network — Chemical (LRN-C) maintains a network of state public health and environmental laboratories capable of detecting chemical threat agents in clinical and environmental specimens. Following COVID-19, the LRN-C suffered attrition in trained chemical testing staff and lapse of proficiency in some network laboratories due to resource reallocation during the pandemic.

This RFP funds LRN-C Level 1 and Level 2 laboratories to rebuild chemical threat agent testing capacity, validate updated analytical methods, and integrate environmental specimen testing (air, water, soil) with clinical specimen workflows to support both terrorism response and environmental health surveillance use cases.

RFP context: RFP ID:** Public Health Labs-RFP-2022-MASSFAT-037 | Issue Date:** June 20, 2022 | Federal Sponsor:** Department of Justice (DOJ) / National Institute of Justice (NIJ) | Program Area:** Forensic Science — Mass Fatality Identification

Mass fatality incidents — wildfires, building collapses, transportation disasters, and mass violence events — increasingly challenge state forensic and public health laboratory systems to perform rapid DNA-based victim identification at scale. The Camp Fire (2018, 85 deaths), the Champlain Towers collapse (2021, 98 deaths), and multiple wildfire seasons have strained state capacity and demonstrated that most state forensic laboratories lack the rapid DVI (Disaster Victim Identification) protocols, reference sample processing pipelines, and CODIS integration pathways required for large-scale identification. This RFP, administered through Public Health Labs in coordination with NIJ, funds state public health and forensic laboratories to build and validate rapid mass fatality DNA identification capability.

RFP context: RFP ID:** Public Health Labs-RFP-2021-FOOD-013 | Issue Date:** August 2, 2021 | Federal Sponsor:** Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / DFWED | Program Area:** Foodborne Disease — PulseNet Laboratory Network

PulseNet, CDC's national molecular subtyping network for foodborne disease surveillance, transitioned from pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) to whole-genome sequencing (WGS) as the national standard. WGS provides dramatically higher resolution for cluster detection and outbreak investigation for Salmonella, STEC O157 and non-O157, Listeria monocytogenes, Campylobacter, and Vibrio. State PulseNet laboratories are the frontline of this system and must sustain WGS throughput, data quality, and turnaround to enable timely national outbreak detection.

This RFP funds state PulseNet laboratories to sustain and enhance their foodborne WGS capacity, improve data completeness, and integrate with FDA's GenomeTrakr network for comprehensive food safety genomic surveillance.

RFP context: RFP ID:** Public Health Labs-RFP-2023-H5N1-023 | Issue Date:** August 14, 2023 | Federal Sponsor:** Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / ICIEID | Program Area:** Influenza — Pandemic Preparedness

H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has caused unprecedented poultry losses in the United States since 2022, with confirmed human cases in agricultural workers representing a critical signal for pandemic preparedness. The U.S. government has accelerated preparedness activities under the National Pandemic Influenza Plans, and state public health laboratories are essential to early detection of human-to-human transmission and case confirmation.

State LRN-B laboratories authorized for influenza A H5 testing currently rely on CDC's influenza laboratory for confirmatory testing. This RFP funds a prioritized subset of state laboratories to implement CDC-authorized H5N1 testing assays, establish agricultural worker surveillance partnerships, and conduct surge exercises simulating multi-state H5N1 case events.
